details.title: Arban – Ornament Study No. 86
details.lead: From Arban's Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons et de saxhorn, first edition, 1864. The notes are the cornet part as printed, in written pitch for the B♭ cornet. Below: the book's own words, translated from the French.
facts: Arban, Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons et de saxhorn, first edition (Paris: Léon Escudier, 1864)

The mordent written out as two small notes before the first eighth of a group of three. 24 bars, with a double bar after bar 8. Bar 6 ends with a quarter and no rest after it in the print; the eighth rest that completes it is added here, as in bar 2.

sections.heading: The mordent
paragraphs: The mordent is nothing but a hurried trill; it needs neither preparation nor resolution. It is marked with a short wavy sign; Example 10 shows the sign and its effect.
The mordent of several beats is nearly impossible on the cornet à pistons. So keep to the mordent of a single beat, which is far easier and very graceful (Example 11).
The mordent takes its length from the very note it belongs to. (See Nos. 81 to 88.)

sections.heading: A word on all of these
paragraphs: Since all the lessons on ornaments were written to serve as studies, I have brought together, on purpose and in abundance, every kind of ornament. But take great care not to overuse them so in practice, for that would be in the worst of taste.

sources.title: IMSLP: Grande méthode complète de cornet à pistons (Arban), first edition, Paris 1864
